title: Missing Slippage Protection on Mint Price and BalancerPooler Liquidity Addition
description: (1) mint() reads config.price at execution time with no maxPrice parameter, enabling front-running since each mint increases the price. (2) BalancerPooler defaults minBptAmountOut to 0 when extraData is empty, making Balancer liquidity additions fully sandwichable.
impact: MEV extraction on every mint. Front-runners can sandwich mint transactions to extract value. BalancerPooler loses value on LP entries.
attackPath: Attacker monitors mempool for mint transactions
Attacker front-runs with their own mint, increasing the price
Victim's mint executes at the higher price
Attacker profits from the price difference
For BalancerPooler: attacker sandwiches addLiquidity calls with minBptAmountOut=0
recommendation: Add a maxPrice parameter to mint() so users can specify maximum acceptable price. Set a meaningful minBptAmountOut in BalancerPooler instead of defaulting to 0.
